ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Rabindranath Tagore Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New-patient visit for a weak stream, straining, and frequent urination at night, with a feeling that the bladder does not empty. Concerns: A weak stream, straining, dribbling, and getting up four times a night for months; lately he passes only small amounts and feels his bladder never empties; Since a severe urinary infection in the hills five months ago he has not felt well; he wants to keep writing and teaching; He fears an operation more than he fears his illness, and wants to know every gentler choice before any surgery is decided. [S]

tr.td: Indwelling urethral catheter inserted (16 French, 10 mL balloon) with a leg bag and night bag; 680 mL drained; observed for two hours for post-obstructive diuresis, which did not occur
Ultrasound of both kidneys and the bladder: no hydronephrosis; kidneys normal in size; bladder wall trabeculated, catheter balloon in place; prostate about 85 mL with a modest median lobe
Change of urethral catheter before cultures for a febrile catheter-associated infection; urine culture taken from the new catheter
Trial without catheter after six weeks of tamsulosin: catheter removed in the early morning; voided small amounts; bladder scan 420 mL; catheter replaced
Second trial without catheter after four months of finasteride with tamsulosin: catheter removed in the early morning; voided 240 mL and 210 mL; bladder scan 150 mL; catheter left out

tr.td: New-patient visit for a weak stream, straining, and frequent urination at night, with a feeling that the bladder does not empty
Two-week review with kidney and bladder ultrasound results and urology consultation
Six-week review with a trial without catheter and a geriatric assessment
Ten-week review: shared decision about treatment and goals of care
Five-month review with a planned second trial without catheter
Same-day sick visit for fever with a urinary catheter

Evaluation: IPSS with the quality-of-life question, bladder scan for post-void residual, urinalysis and urine culture, blood count, creatinine and electrolytes, digital rectal examination, and a kidney and bladder ultrasound for obstruction; a frequency-volume chart once voiding

PSA only after shared decision-making: it helps estimate prostate size and choose treatment; screening for prostate cancer is not recommended at his age, and he would not want treatment for a slow-growing cancer; drawn before the catheter is placed, because retention and catheters raise it

Indwelling urethral catheter to drain the bladder, with a closed drainage system, the bag below the bladder, daily washing with soap and water, no routine antibiotics or bladder washouts, no treatment of bacteria in the urine without symptoms, a change every four weeks, and same-day review for fever, pain, blood, or a blocked catheter

Tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime for at least three days and usually several weeks before a trial without catheter; fall precautions: take it after the evening meal, rise slowly, sit to pass urine at night, and use a night light

Urology consultation for chronic urinary retention with a raised creatinine: confirm the cause, judge the risk, plan the trial without catheter, advise on a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor, and set out the procedures that suit a frail 79-year-old who wants to avoid an operation

Medication review with the AGS Beers Criteria: avoid anticholinergic drugs for bladder symptoms while in retention, first-generation antihistamines, and benzodiazepines; avoid nonselective alpha-blockers; review his herbal preparation with the pharmacist for interactions and unlabeled ingredients

Monitor on the CMID and AUA schedule: IPSS at every visit once voiding; post-void residual with each trial without catheter and after it; creatinine with retention; PSA at baseline and six months after starting finasteride, doubled for interpretation; response to tamsulosin at four to twelve weeks and to finasteride at three to six months
Geriatric assessment before any surgical decision: frailty, gait and falls, orthostatic blood pressure on tamsulosin, cognition, mood, delirium risk, nutrition, and what matters most to him

Finasteride 5 mg daily for the 85 mL prostate, with a new PSA baseline after six months (measured value doubled for interpretation); trial without catheter after about six weeks of tamsulosin, once any infection is treated

Surgical options counseled after the failed trial without catheter: laser enucleation (HoLEP) recommended for an 85 mL prostate with refractory retention; transurethral resection and simple prostatectomy as alternatives; prostatic artery embolization under local anesthesia as a less invasive option with less durable results; prostatic urethral lift and water vapor therapy less suitable for this size, median lobe, and retention; each weighed against his frailty, delirium risk, and wishes

His decision, in his own terms: defer any operation or procedure; keep the catheter, changed every four weeks, with tamsulosin and finasteride; a second trial without catheter after three to four months of finasteride; reconsider prostatic artery embolization, then laser enucleation, if that fails or if infections recur, bleeding, stones, or kidney harm develop; continue his herbal preparation after the pharmacist's review
Bladder drained and kidney function back to normal within two weeks
Creatinine 1.42 mg/dL at presentation, 1.18 mg/dL after two weeks of drainage; no hydronephrosis
No catheter-associated infection, or prompt treatment if one occurs
One febrile catheter-associated infection at four weeks, treated in clinic for 7 days without admission; resolved
A treatment decision that he understands and that fits his values, after a geriatric assessment, by about ten weeks
Chose to continue the catheter with tamsulosin and finasteride and to try again without the catheter after three to four months, deferring surgery; recorded in his own words
Voiding without a catheter, with a post-void residual under 300 mL, by about five months
Second trial without catheter succeeded: residual 150 mL, IPSS 13
Goals of care and a health care agent recorded
Goals of care discussed at the ten-week visit; health care agent named and his wishes recorded at the wellness visit

list.item: Independent in bathing, dressing, eating, and transfers; walks slowly indoors without an aid; needs help with travel and heavy housework; up four times a night to pass urine, which leaves him tired by day [S]

Tall, white-bearded, courteous, and articulate, with a dry humor; mood "patient, but tired of my own body"; worried about losing his independence and about an operation; thinking clear and well organized; no depression or thoughts of self-harm [S]
